analysis:
Tesla fell 10.1%, 5.6 points more than the market and 7.2 points more than its mega-cap tech peers, marking this as a company-specific decline rather than a shared move within the theme. The coverage centers on a post-midterm plunge tied to a Democratic sweep, with headlines discussing investigations into Trump, questions about merger prospects and AI build-out, and roughly $450 billion in value lost across Tesla and SpaceX; one item mentions the stock trading at Apple's valuation, while another covers a robotics competitor beginning to trade after a SPAC merger. 

Tesla reports earnings in 83 days, on January 27. The stock's typical move around earnings beyond the market is 2.8 percentage points, though across the last seven reports, beating estimates has not reliably led to gains—two of three beats were followed by negative abnormal moves, and the stock fell after three beats overall.
